newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Jly wheat sets new 10-1/2 mo high, crop loss.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Jly wheat sets new 10-1/2 mo high, crop loss.

text.p: New crop July CBOT wheat surged to a fresh 10-1/2 month high Friday and all contracts closed strongly higher on escalating concerns about crop losses in the U.S. and in the European Community, especially in France, traders said.
"There are all kinds of horror stories and they pulled some rain out of Europe. All of a sudden we've gone from bearish to bullish in a week," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
The July contract jumped to a session high of $4.47 per bushel which is a new 10-1/2-month high for that month.

On May 28 last year, July reached $4.47 per bushel and the contract high for that month of $4.65 was set on April 11, 1996. The recent high of $4.38 was set during the opening of futures trading Tuesday. July moved in a 21 cent range Friday.

Traders cited persistent talk that the weekend freeze in the U.S. Great Plains may have damaged up to 200 million bushels of wheat. The market rallied the 20-cent limit Monday then tumbled on reports a widely-followed analytical firm pegged the losses at only roughly 50 million bushels.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 13-1/2 cents higher with May up 11-3/4 at $4.37 and July up 13-1/2 at $4.44-1/2.
Crop specialists Friday told Reuters that last week's freeze may have sliced more than 100 million bushels from the Kansas wheat crop and severe losses in Oklahoma also were likely.

"Those numbers for Kansas alone are not unrealistic," said Rollie Sears, a Kansas State University wheat breeder, who this week toured the damaged areas. "The damage in the southern third of the state is worse than I thought."
The market also took note of potential cold weather in the state again next week.

"We will have to keep our eye on next week," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass. "It looks like it will continue to cool off in the HRW (hard red winter wheat) belt."
Wheat futures surged Thursday on news the EU halted its weekly export tender program for wheat amid concerns about dry weather in Europe, especially France, the key wheat growing nation.
French weather forecasters on Friday predicted another five days without rain across most of France's farm districts.
Patrick Galois, forecaster with national weather service Meteo France, saw no rain on the horizon in northern France where most wheat, barley and sugar is grown.
LIT America bought five million bushels of July, E.D. and F. Man International bought three million bushels of July and LFG Futures bought 2.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Merrill Lynch Futures and Cargill Inc each sold two million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 31,000 contracts, above the 27,318 posted Thursday.

In wheat options, Paine Webber bought 600 September $4.20 calls at 47-1/2 cents and sold 600 September $5.20 calls at 15-1/2 cents, traders said. Cargill Investor Services bought 400 July $4.20 puts and sold 400 July $3.90 puts at 10 cents, traders said. CIS also bought 300 July $4.00 puts and sold 300 July $3.80 puts at five cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, below the 17,383 traded Thursday.
